description: Stochastic sequencer: sixteen sliders weight how often each of sixteen voltages is picked, and a clock draws one of them at random each time

params.text: Sets how often its voltage is picked against the others, 0 to 100; a slider at zero takes its voltage out of the draw
The chance that a draw is a rest rather than a note, 0 to 1
Sets the seed the random generator takes on a reset, 0 to 1

inputs.text: Each rising edge draws a new voltage; the channel count here sets how many sequences run side by side
A rising edge reseeds the random generator from the Seed value, so the same sequence comes back
The sixteen voltages the draw picks from, one per channel; with nothing patched they are a chromatic scale in twelfths of a volt
Sets the seed, 0-10V across the whole range, and overrides the Seed knob when a reset arrives
Sets the rest chance, 0-10V across the whole range, one channel per sequence, and overrides the Rest knob while patched
Sets all sixteen weights at once, one channel per slider, 0-10V across the whole range
Sets the weight of its voltage, 0-10V across the whole range, and overrides that slider while patched

outputs.text: The drawn voltage, one channel per sequence; through a rest it holds its last value unless the menu says otherwise
Passes the clock through on a sequence's channel while that draw is a note, and stays at 0V through a rest
A 1ms trigger on a sequence's channel when a draw lands on a different voltage than the one before

notes: every slider comes up at zero; until the weights add up to two or more, every draw lands on the first voltage
menu: Hold CV on Rest — holds the last voltage through rests; turned off, the CV output follows the drawn voltage even through a rest

inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
